conventions.convention: AC is assumed for the conditional-expectation existence convention. Time is discrete, with filtration indexed from zero and observations indexed from one; no completed filtration is required.

The conditional mgf bound holds for every time and every fixed real λ, with an exceptional null set allowed to depend on time and λ. The deterministic proxy σ² is strictly positive and need not equal the variance; independence and identical distribution are not assumed.
ρ>0, α∈(0,1), v≥0, and uα(v)=√((v+ρ)log((v+ρ)/(α²ρ))). The interval endpoints are included and C₀=ℝ; the interval definition alone asserts no coverage.
The mixing law is N(0,1/ρ), so ρ is its precision. The Gaussian integral formula includes v=0.

Confidence intervals are intersected with Θ and C₀=Θ. Coverage is pointwise in θ under Pθ, simultaneous over integer times, with a common process, filtration and known proxy; Θ needs no measurable structure.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC. On a discrete filtered probability space, a real adapted process has conditionally sub-Gaussian increments around μ∈ℝ with proxy σ²>0 when, for every integer t≥1 and fixed λ∈ℝ, exp(λ(Xt−μ)) is integrable and E[exp(λ(Xt−μ)) | F(t−1)]≤exp(λ²σ²/2) almost surely; the exceptional null set may depend on t and λ.

Assume AC and the conditional sub-Gaussian model around μ with known proxy σ²>0. For ρ>0, S₀(μ)=0, St(μ)=Σ(i=1,…,t)(Xi−μ), and Vt=tσ², Mt(μ)=√(ρ/(Vt+ρ))exp(St(μ)²/[2(Vt+ρ)]) is a nonnegative test supermartingale for {P}, with M₀(μ)=1.

Assume AC and the conditional sub-Gaussian model around μ∈ℝ with proxy σ²>0. For each fixed λ∈ℝ, Ltλ(μ)=exp(λSt(μ)−λ²tσ²/2), with S₀(μ)=0, is a nonnegative test supermartingale for {P}, with L₀λ(μ)=1.
Assume AC. For ρ>0, v≥0, s∈ℝ, and πρ=N(0,1/ρ), ∫ exp(λs−vλ²/2) πρ(dλ)=√(ρ/(v+ρ))exp(s²/[2(v+ρ)]).
For α∈(0,1), ρ>0, v≥0 and s∈ℝ, M(v,s)=√(ρ/(v+ρ))exp(s²/[2(v+ρ)]) satisfies M(v,s)≥1/α if and only if |s|≥uα(v).

Assume AC, Θ⊆ℝ, a common discrete filtered measurable space, laws (Pθ)θ∈Θ and a common real adapted process whose increments under every Pθ are conditionally sub-Gaussian around θ with the same known proxy σ²>0. For ρ>0 and α∈(0,1), C₀=Θ and Ct=Θ∩[X̄t−uα(tσ²)/t, X̄t+uα(tσ²)/t] satisfy Pθ(θ∈Ct for every t≥0)≥1−α for every θ∈Θ.

seams_checked.note: Checked the supplier's finite-horizon lemma and discrete Ville theorem against the consumer's F4 and Steps 2.1–3.1. The consumer carries AC, uses a nonnegative test supermartingale with initial value one under each fixed Pθ, and invokes the stated supremum bound at α∈(0,1). Closed-interval exclusion gives |St(θ)|>uα(tσ²), hence threshold crossing; no equality between the crossing and supremum events is assumed. The supplier proves the stronger supremum bound using lower thresholds, so the cited direction and conclusion are supported.
